title: ₹33 Paracetamol at ₹408, study exposes Indian private hospital markups on medicines
content: Medicines and medical supplies at private hospitals are being billed at steep markups, with prices in some cases soaring several-fold over their actual cost, according to a recent study. For instance, a paracetamol priced at 32.80 is being charged at up to 408, while doxycycline, an antibiotic that costs 118.50, is being billed at as much as 920. Colistimethate sodium, which costs 715, is similarly charged at up to 5,385, according to the study by the Jan Swasthya Abhiyan's (JSA) Working Group on 'Access to Medicines and Treatment'. The study, which covered five major private hospital chains in the country, also found that an oxygen mask priced at 55 costs patients 310 to 650 at private hospitals. A needle costing just 63 paise is billed at 3.60 to 4.40, while a PPE kit priced at 175 is charged at 215 to 800. Besides medicines, hospitals also charge markups of 200% to 400% on medical supplies such as syringes and IV sets. Bed charges soar As per 2024-25 figures, hospitals charged an average of 60,000 to 78,000 per bed per day, including various charges. In 2025-26, the daily charge rose to as much as 78,000. The study estimates that hospitals are targeting annual revenue of around 23 lakh per bed, excluding charges for medical examinations, medicines and consulation fees for doctors. In contrast, hospitals such as CMC Vellore, which treat serious illnesses, charge only around 28,781, including treatment costs, the report notes.
